main_text.l: Argos hîc cognominatur, Lyncei filius eft, & pater Talai
à quo natus eft Adraftus, qui Argos incoluit, Argiuorum
& Sycionorum rex.
Τοιαῦτα μὴν.) Epilogus oraculi Amphiarai.
Χαίρων ὃ ἡ αὐτὸς.) Scholion verba ait esse victoris, quod-
que vsus sit Aristomenes oraculo Alcmanis de futura vi-
ctoria, eiusque domui coniunctum fuisse Alcmanis facel-
lum. Verùm puto poëtæ esse verba, breuiter laudantis he-
roa Alcmanem: nam & coronare ipsum & aspergere hym-
no ait, quod non est Aristomanis, sed poëtæ officium.
Τίτων ὅτι μοι.) Ratio poëtæ, cur & hunc celebret, quia vi-
cinus mihi. 2. patronus fortunarum mearum, forte Thebis
cultus est. 3. Delphos euntì successum debitum occurrit. 4.
Artes vatidicas mihi communicauit, aut in me oraculi sui
certitudinem confirmauit.
Strophe 4. versuum 9.
ORationem ad Apollinem conuertit, duas Aristome-
nis victorias illi acceptas ferens, commendaturus illi
poëticen suam & fortunas victoris.
Τὸ ἐκατηβόλε.) Inuocatio poëtæ ad Apollinem κατ'
ἐπιμβολὼ. Templum Apollinis Delphicum παντόξιον dicitur,
quia aduenas quoscunque admittat. Apollo ἑκατηβόλος di-
citur, procul iaculàs, quod ad radios solares transfert Ma-
crobius. est idem epitheton etiam Musis tributum suprà
in 9. Olymp. Strophe 1. ἀλλὰ νῦν ἑκατηβόλων μοῖσαν ὑπὸ τόξων.
Τὸ μὴν μέγιστον.) Victoriam praesentem Pythicam Apolli-
ni tanquam autori acceptam refert.
Οἴκοι ὃ παρόδεν.) Altera victoria Aristomenis quam in Æ-
gina obtinuit: coluère hîpræcipuè Apollinè & Mincruâ.
ac in Apollinis gratiam instituti erant ludi Delphinia di-
cti, qui constabant quinquercio. in his vicit, antequam
ad Pythica proficisceretur spectacula. ὑμῶν pro σῶς tuis:
Apollinis enim festum erat.
Ἑνόντ' ἀλ' εὐχομαι.) Propositionem subiunctúrus δύχω ex-
plicat.
Antistrophe 4. versuum 9.
DVo commendat Apollini, suos hymnos & fortunas
Aristomenis. inde longiùs digreditur in vulgi iudicium

page.notes: Greek passages are only approximately set in this transcription; the Greek type is worn and several words are doubtful and should be checked against the scan. Lines of the Greek at the start of notes, and the Greek in the Strophe glosses, are not reliable. The first word of the Greek note "Τοιαῦτα μὴν" and the marginal Greek lines are marked by the scan only partially. Some printed spellings (e.g. "s" forms, "Scholion") are kept as printed where legible. The closing initials "T.J." are printed at the foot of the text.
